headline: Blood is your body's river—delivering oxygen, nutrients, and immune cells everywhere
universal_truth: Distribution systems are as important as what they distribute
fun_facts: Your blood travels about 12,000 miles per day—that's nearly halfway around Earth
You have about 25 trillion red blood cells; your body makes 2 million new ones every second
A single drop of blood contains millions of cells doing different jobs
discussion_questions: What are the 'blood rivers' in your life that distribute what you need?
How does knowing blood travels 12,000 miles daily change your view of your body?
What happens when distribution systems fail?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Right now, a river is flowing through you. Five liters of blood, circulating through 60,000 miles of vessels, delivering oxygen to every cell, picking up waste, fighting infections, healing wounds. Your blood is busier than you are.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Blood does many jobs—but how? A single drop contains millions of different cells. What's actually in blood, and how does one fluid handle so many critical tasks?
cliff.prompt: What are the main components of blood?

options.text: Red cells for oxygen, white cells for immunity, platelets for clotting, and plasma as carrier
options.response: Yes. Blood is a mix of specialized cells suspended in plasma, each with a crucial role.

options.text: Blood is mostly water with some iron for carrying oxygen
options.response: Plasma is mostly water, but blood contains much more...

q1.title: The Oxygen Fleet
q1.script: Red blood cells are oxygen couriers. Your 25 trillion red cells, each packed with hemoglobin, carry oxygen from lungs to tissues and carbon dioxide back. Your body produces 2 million new red cells every second to keep the fleet running.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Oxygen Fleet"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Defense Force
q2.script: White blood cells are your immune army—fewer in number but crucial. They patrol the bloodstream hunting pathogens, remembering past invaders, and coordinating immune responses. You carry a security force in every drop of blood.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: The Repair Crew
q3.script: Platelets are tiny cell fragments that stop bleeding. When you're cut, platelets rush to the site, stick together, and form clots. Without them, a papercut could be fatal. Your body has a built-in construction crew for damage repair.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Distribution is essential. Blood reminds us that it's not enough to have resources—you need systems to move them where they're needed. Circulation matters. Build pathways that deliver.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 80—80 days of learning! Tomorrow, we'll explore how you see the world. Until then, appreciate the 12,000 miles your blood is traveling today.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Distribution Audit - Are Resources Reaching Where Needed?
growTrack.learning_objective: Evaluate whether your resources reach where they're needed
growTrack.activity: Like blood, you have resources—time, energy, attention—that need to reach the right places. Are they flowing to where they're most needed? Identify one 'organ' in your life that's not receiving what it needs and redirect some flow.
